feat(dashboards): show widget placeholders on shared dashboards (2/4) (#61416)

## Problem

Shared dashboards previously hid widget tiles entirely or showed empty space. Viewers couldn't see that a dashboard includes error tracking or session replay widgets, and the frontend still attempted widget data fetches that shared pages cannot satisfy.

## Changes

- Show widget tiles on **Public** shared dashboards with a PostHoggy placeholder body and per-widget copy (error tracking vs session replay)
- Serialize **metadata-only** widget payloads on shared dashboards (`id`, `widget_type`, `name`, `description`, `config`) — no user fields or query results
- Skip `run_widgets` fetches on Public/Export placements; enable widget rendering on shared pages when tile metadata is present (shared pages don't receive team feature flags)
- Hide widget tiles on Export placement (PNG/embed exports)

## How did you test this code?

Automated tests (agent-authored; no manual browser verification in this session):

- `dashboardLogic.test.ts` — public placement skips widget fetch; widgets enabled when tile metadata present
- `DashboardWidgetItem.test.tsx` — shared placeholder renders per-widget copy
- `test_dashboard_widgets.py::test_shared_dashboard_tile_serializer_omits_widget_payload`
- `test_sharing.py::TestSharedCohortInlining::test_shared_dashboard_includes_widget_metadata_only`

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

No docs changes in this PR — behavior is additive for shared dashboard rendering.

## 🤖 Agent context

Agent-assisted PR (Cursor). Builds on the dashboard widget stack (error tracking + session replay widgets).

Key decisions:
- Shared widget data path lives in `SharingViewSet` with `is_shared=True`; removed dead share-token guards on `DashboardsViewSet` that could never fire
- Public shared pages bypass the `dashboard-widgets` feature flag when exported tile metadata exists, since shared exports don't include team feature flags
- Placeholder copy is catalog-driven so new widget types can define their own shared messaging

Known follow-up (not in this PR): widget/insight tiles with overlapping grid coordinates may render in a different visual order on shared dashboards vs the private editor.

feat(dashboards): add slo for widget data delivery (3/4) (#61431)

## Problem

Dashboard widgets fetch live data via `run_widgets`, but we had no SLO coverage for whether that delivery succeeds — unlike subscriptions, alerts, and query service.

## Changes

- Add `SloOperation.DASHBOARD_WIDGET_DELIVERY` and register it on the analytics platform SLO monitoring dashboard (99.95% target, US + EU)
- Wrap each widget query in `run_widgets` with `slo_operation`, tagging `widget_type`, `dashboard_id`, and `tile_id`
- Success = query returned data; failure = query raised (same path that returns the generic error to the client)

Access/validation failures (missing tile, product access, API scope) are intentionally excluded — those are not platform delivery failures.

## How did you test this code?

Automated tests (agent-authored):

- `posthog/slo/test/test_slo_context.py` — existing SLO helper coverage
- `test_run_widgets.py::test_run_widgets_emits_slo_on_successful_widget_delivery`
- `test_run_widgets.py::test_run_widgets_emits_slo_failure_when_widget_query_raises`

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

No docs changes — internal observability only.

## 🤖 Agent context

Agent-assisted PR (Cursor). Follows the same `slo_operation` pattern as subscription create and query service, scoped to the actual widget query execution in `_run_widget_query` so we can break down delivery reliability by `widget_type` on the existing SLO monitoring terraform dashboard.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)
